citation.title: Scaling atom-by-atom inverse design using nano-topology optimization and diffusion models

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For a fixed-mass nanocantilever, the generic-layout diffusion model's best sampled design has normalized stiffness 0.736, below the 0.820 best classical Nano-TO design.
claim.location: Results, thickness-periodic nanocantilevers using c-DDPM, Figure 3a
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical and ML runtimes are printed for a comparable design task; no factor can be derived.
claim.alternatives: The Nano-TO-trained TO-DDPM later reaches best stiffness 0.860 versus 0.820 for Nano-TO (Figure 3b); the abstract qualitatively says diffusion candidates approach the optimization frontier, while Nano-TO exceeds continuum TO on nanopillars.

baseline.classical_method: Atomistic Nano-TO for nanocantilevers, and continuum FEM-TO for nanopillars (Results; Supplementary Note A.14)
baseline.implementation: Nano-TO atomistic optimizer and conditional DDPM code released in the linked repository; continuum FEM-TO based on the 169-line MATLAB code of Liu and Tovar (Supplementary Note A.14)
baseline.problem_size: 100×300 binary cross-sectional image for thickness-periodic nanocantilevers; 148,500 active atoms and 1,980 passive clamp atoms for similarity analysis (Methods; Supplementary Note A.9)
baseline.classical_iterations: Nano-TO optimization stops at compute budget; number for selected cantilever comparison not stated (Methods)
baseline.data_generation_cost: Gaussian-DDPM uses 32,000 valid synthetic layouts; TO-DDPM retains 32,000 connected designs from 48,000 Nano-TO outputs; generation time not stated (Results, c-DDPM)
baseline.quality_metric: Atomistic bending stiffness of each returned design, normalized to initial beam, at fixed 59.60% mass ratio (Results, Figure 3)
baseline.quality_gap: Best Gaussian-DDPM design: 0.736 versus best Nano-TO 0.820 normalized stiffness, about 10.2% lower [inferred]; TO-DDPM later reaches 0.860, about 4.9% higher [inferred] (Results, Figure 3)

R1.evidence: Results, Figure 3a: selected comparison measures stiffness at fixed mass rather than speed.

R2.evidence: Results, Figure 3a: selected comparison gives no classical versus ML timing.

R3.evidence: Results, Figure 3a: selected claim is quality-only; no quantified speed claim for it.

R4.evidence: Results, c-DDPM and Methods: generated candidates are mapped back to atomistic structures and stiffness tested at fixed mass; disconnected layouts are filtered from training and invalid synthetic layouts are rejected, but generated-design failure rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 32,000 generated samples per selected DDPM run, at one 59.60% target mass ratio; additional atomistic beam and pillar design settings (Results)

notes: The abstract's continuum-TO comparison concerns the non-learned Nano-TO method. The primary ML-versus-classical quantitative comparison is the first DDPM versus Nano-TO result in the main text. Public code is stated, but the paper does not give a directly runnable timed benchmark or licence terms for this retest criterion.
